reasoning:
Recent public polling on Nebraska’s 2026 U.S. Senate race shows a genuinely competitive contest between independent Dan Osborn and Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, but all of the polling is from May and earlier and is either Osborn-sponsored or highlighted as partisan, and there are no new head‑to‑head numbers from the last 45 days.[1][3][14] Within the last 45 days, credible outlets and forecasters instead frame the race using older polling and structural context: Cook Political Report rates the seat Solid Republican, Nebraska is a strongly Republican state (Trump +20, R+23 PVI), and syntheses of the early polling and fundamentals point to a small Republican edge of roughly **R+2 to R+3** in a Ricketts–Osborn general‑election matchup.[3][13][15] Because the only explicit numeric “current margin” grounded in recent analysis rather than fresh polling is the battleground overview’s prediction of **Ricketts +2**, the best evidence‑based point estimate for the present general‑election margin is **R+2**, with the caveat that it relies on extrapolations from older Osborn‑sponsored polling rather than new independent surveys.

No credible, state-specific Nebraska presidential polling for the 2026 cycle appears in the last 45 days, so there is no current presidential margin to report for Nebraska; all structural indicators and commentary treat the state as safely Republican but without fresh numbers.[13][15]

sources.name: New York Times – Nebraska U.S. Senate Election 2026: Latest Polls
sources.details: New York Times’ Nebraska 2026 Senate polling page summarizes Tavern Research and other Osborn-aligned or partisan polls from May and earlier, showing a mix of Osborn leads and narrow Ricketts leads but no new head-to-head polling within the last 45 days.

sources.name: Newsweek
sources.details: Newsweek reports on a Tavern Research poll of 1,165 likely Nebraska voters sponsored by Osborn’s side, finding Osborn 47% to Ricketts 42%, a 5-point Osborn lead, emphasizing the race’s competitiveness in a strongly Republican state.

sources.name: IVN
sources.details: IVN commentary on the Nebraska Senate race describes recent head-to-head polling as close and mostly Osborn-sponsored, noting a poll with Osborn +5 and an earlier poll with Ricketts +1, and stressing that no survey shows the Republican clearly ahead despite Trump’s 20-point win in Nebraska.

sources.name: Yahoo News – U.S. Senate Battlegrounds in 2026: 12 Races to Watch
sources.details: A battleground overview of the 2026 Senate races characterizes Nebraska as a race Democrats cannot win but where independent Dan Osborn is the main challenger, recalls his 7-point loss in 2024 and early competitive polls, and offers an explicit prediction of Pete Ricketts (R) +2 in the 2026 general election.

sources.name: Polymarket – Nebraska Senate Margin of Victory 2026
sources.details: A Polymarket prediction market on Nebraska’s 2026 Senate margin of victory synthesizes recent public polling and structural factors, notes Cook Political Report’s Solid Republican rating, and shows the most heavily traded outcome as a Republican margin of 3–6%, implying expectations of a narrow Ricketts win even though individual polls are close.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Nebraska statewide PVI
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index assigns Nebraska a rating of R+23, indicating the state votes about 23 percentage points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections and underscoring the strongly Republican structural environment for both Senate and presidential contests.

sources.name: Nebraska Examiner – Ricketts outraises Osborn in latest report for Nebraska US Senate race
sources.details: Nebraska Examiner reports that Ricketts raised $6.3 million from April through June, more than triple Osborn’s haul, highlighting a significant Republican fundraising advantage that complements the state’s GOP-leaning fundamentals rather than providing a direct vote margin.

sources.name: Ballotpedia – Nebraska set to have a second straight U.S. Senate election without both major parties on the ballot
sources.details: Ballotpedia explains that Democratic nominee Cindy Burbank, who won the May 12 primary, withdrew from the 2026 Nebraska Senate race on July 17 and was formally removed from the ballot on July 21, leaving Ricketts (R), Osborn (nonpartisan), and Marvin (Legal Marijuana Now) as the general-election candidates, clarifying the structure of the race but not its polling margin.
sources.date_range: May 12, 2026 primary; July 17-21, 2026 withdrawal and ballot decisions

sources.name: NBC News – Nebraska Senate Primary Election 2026 Results
sources.details: NBC News’ Nebraska primary results page shows Pete Ricketts winning the Republican Senate primary overwhelmingly and Cindy Burbank winning the Democratic primary by a wide margin before her later withdrawal, underscoring Ricketts’ strength within the GOP but not providing general-election vote-share polling.
